question_text:
A 13-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of worsening fever, headache, photophobia, and nausea for 2 days. One week ago, she returned from summer camp. She has received all age-appropriate immunizations. Her temperature is 39.1°C (102.3°F). She is oriented to person, place, and time. Physical examination shows a maculopapular rash. There is rigidity of the neck; forced flexion of the neck results in involuntary flexion of the knees and hips. Cerebrospinal fluid studies show:
Opening pressure 120 mm H2O
Appearance Clear
Protein 47 mg/dL
Glucose 68 mg/dL
White cell count 280/mm3
Segmented neutrophils 15%
Lymphocytes 85%
Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?"?

                    ### Question
                    A 13-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of worsening fever, headache, photophobia, and nausea for 2 days. One week ago, she returned from summer camp. She has received all age-appropriate immunizations. Her temperature is 39.1°C (102.3°F). She is oriented to person, place, and time. Physical examination shows a maculopapular rash. There is rigidity of the neck; forced flexion of the neck results in involuntary flexion of the knees and hips. Cerebrospinal fluid studies show:
Opening pressure 120 mm H2O
Appearance Clear
Protein 47 mg/dL
Glucose 68 mg/dL
White cell count 280/mm3
Segmented neutrophils 15%
Lymphocytes 85%
Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?"?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Echovirus
opb. Listeria monocytogenes
opc. Herpes simplex virus
opd. Streptococcus pneumoniae

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The clinical presentation of fever, headache, photophobia, nausea, neck rigidity, and a maculopapular rash, combined with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings of clear appearance, high lymphocyte count, normal glucose, and elevated protein, is indicative of viral meningitis. The high percentage of lymphocytes (85%) and normal glucose levels in the CSF are characteristic of viral rather than bacterial meningitis. Among the viral causes, Echovirus is a common cause of viral meningitis in children and is associated with outbreaks in settings like summer camps. The evidence paths support the association of viral meningitis with viruses, including Echoviruses, aligning with the consensus that Echovirus is a likely causal organism in this scenario. Other options like Listeria monocytogenes, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Neisseria meningitidis are more commonly associated with bacterial meningitis, which typically presents with a higher neutrophil count and lower glucose levels in the CSF. Herpes simplex virus can cause viral meningitis but is less commonly associated with the described setting and presentation. Therefore, the most likely causal organism is Echovirus.
